normalization.overview: AI LABS explains Leon Lin's design workflow: strong references, target mockups, a quality bar, repeated criticism and the Cook skill. The Reader separates an inspectable iteration process from subjective quality scores.
normalization.whyItMatters: Coding agents can deliver functioning interfaces whose visual hierarchy, responsiveness and accessibility are poor. Reference-based comparison can expose gaps, but an arbitrary similarity percentage cannot certify product quality.
normalization.ghostMeshTakeaway: Use owner-selected references, repeatable screenshots, specific criticism, responsive and accessibility checks, and a cost-bounded revision ledger. Keep final aesthetic and operational acceptance with humans.
normalization.falsification: Run matched UI tasks with the same agent/model budget, blind user ratings, accessibility checks, review time, total cost, and stable test devices; compare reference-driven Cook iterations against ordinary bounded review.
normalization.freshness: November 2026 creator video and current Cook repository inspected. Public automatic captions support bounded paraphrase, not visually certified demonstration or replicated quality outcomes.

claims.proposition: Strong visual references provide more actionable design constraints than generic descriptive prompts.
claims.assessment: The video demonstrates a reference-first instruction pattern, but no controlled accuracy comparison.
claims.limits: A reference may still be inappropriate, inaccessible or copied too literally.

claims.proposition: Mockups before full implementation can reduce rework and unnecessary agent effort.
claims.assessment: The presenter recommends a visible target before building. Time and token savings are not independently measured.
claims.limits: Benefit depends on the task, mockup quality and how much implementation work is avoided.

claims.proposition: A 99% or 99.9% target reliably measures visual quality.
claims.assessment: Cook explicitly calls 99.9% an aspirational, probably unreachable stretch goal rather than a validated metric.
claims.limits: Human/model similarity ratings are subjective; only selected dimensions such as color delta are command-measured.

claims.proposition: The tutorial's self-rated result near 66% is an objective quality measurement.
claims.assessment: The creator discusses a lower assessed result but supplies no independently calibrated universal similarity measurement.
claims.limits: No blinded repeatability, population validity or measured perceptual threshold established.

claims.proposition: Longer autonomous agent runs systematically produce better design outcomes.
claims.assessment: The documented Cook loop sets time floors for ambitious demonstrations and repeated revisions.
claims.limits: Marginal quality improvement, inference cost and model token consumption are not controlled in this video.

claims.proposition: A prohibition list alone can eliminate generic AI design.
claims.assessment: The source advocates rejecting recurring aesthetic tropes. A list can be useful as targeted feedback, not as a universal design theory.
claims.limits: Style appropriateness is contextual; some banned elements may be correct for a specific identity.

claims.proposition: Building one section and then motion incrementally improves reviewability.
claims.assessment: The source recommends staged construction so individual defects can be corrected.
claims.limits: No controlled comparison demonstrates that a staged process always saves effort.

claims.proposition: Fresh-context AI critics provide an independent and reliable stop signal.
claims.assessment: The creator skill uses fresh-context side-by-side critics with median scoring and calibration notes.
claims.limits: Correlated model bias and uncertain aesthetic rubrics can yield consistently wrong scores.

claims.proposition: Cook specifies a reproducible visual build/compare/critic/fix procedure.
claims.assessment: The public repository specifies a brief, shots, stills, comparison images and a rounds ledger.
claims.limits: An implemented procedure does not prove the resulting product is excellent or accessible.

relationships.reason: Reader #50 questions how polished AI websites converge into a generic visual language. Cook proposes visual references and iterative criticism as a response, while neither source establishes objective taste measurement.

Reader #53 shows why a narrow responsive fix requires direct visual and accessibility checks. Cook expands the iteration idea, but aspirational critic scores cannot substitute for actual device and text-scaling validation.

Reader #55 separates a creator demonstration from sustained workflow proof. The same boundary applies to Cook: repository mechanics are inspectable, while comparative product-quality outcomes remain unverified.
